Title: Inspirit AI Ethical Innovation Summer Opportunity
Summary: Inspirit AI is an online 25-hour guided research program where high school students design applied AI projects in health systems, sustainability, and civic leadership under the mentorship of graduate researchers from Stanford and MIT. During the program students will learn about fundamental AI concepts and tools and complete a mentor-led socially impactful AI project in a domain of interest such as healthcare, finance, psychology, art, among others. No programming experience required, and students with prior coding experience are placed in an advanced cohort.

Title: New York Times Summer Academy
Summary: The Summer Academy at the New York Times offers a 2-week residential or commuter pre-college experience to explore the field of journalism. The program is open to students in grades 10-12 as well as graduating seniors. Whether interested in media, culture, sports, fashion, business, or law, participants investigate the forces shaping these industries under the guidance of seasoned journalists, editors, and media professionals. Each Summer Academy course introduces students to core journalism and media literacy skills, while tapping into their individual interests, from writing to digital storytelling. The program goes beyond the classroom, taking students into newsrooms and local communities to uncover the stories behind compelling headlines.

Title: Technovation Girls App Competition
Summary: The Technovation Girls Competition challenges women under 18 to develop mobile or web applications that solve community or global problems. Eligible teams submit their apps to a global competition for a chance to win awards and scholarships through Quarterfinal, Semifinal, and Final rounds, culminating at the World Summit. Although the formal competition restricts participation by age and gender, the underlying educational curriculum is freely available to learners of all demographics.

Title: Wharton Moneyball Academy Summer Program
Summary: The Wharton Moneyball Academy is a 3-week, on-campus program for rising juniors and seniors with a strong math background and an interest in sports. The program is highly selective with only 75 spots offered. Sponsored by the Wharton Sports Analytics and Business Initiative (WSABI), the Moneyball Academy primes students to become leaders in an increasingly data-driven economy. The curriculum draws from several Wharton Statistics courses and includes hands-on coding in R, the programming language used by professional statisticians. Students collaborate on a final data analytics project, with the chance to be published in the Wharton Sports Analytics Journal. This program is ideal for students with a strong background in math and a love of sports. An interest in computer programming is strongly recommended but no specific background is necessary. All participants who complete the program will earn a Wharton Global Youth Certificate of Completion.

Title: Wharton Data Science Academy Summer Program
Summary: The Wharton Data Science Academy provides a 3-week, on-campus experience for rising juniors and seniors. The program is highly selective with only 75 spots available. The curriculum mirrors the rigor of upper-level Wharton undergraduate courses, while being taught in a way that is accessible to motivated high school learners. Students start from the foundations, including data wrangling and visualization, fundamental probability and statistics (distributions, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing), and core modeling (simple & multiple regression, classification, model assessment). From there, students build steadily toward modern machine learning and artificial intelligence (AI). Coursework is hands-on, using R as the primary language, with selective use of Python (e.g., Colab) for deep learning and LLM. All participants who complete the program will earn a Wharton Global Youth Certificate of Completion.

Title: Wharton Leadership in the Business World Summer Program
Summary: Wharton Leadership in the Business World is a 3-week, on-campus program exclusively for rising seniors (current 11th graders). The program is selective with around 120 spots available. Leadership in the Business World is a three-week immersive program that provides students with a strong foundation in business fundamentals and organizational strategy. Participants engage in team-based projects, simulations, and debates while learning to analyze internal and external business environments using essential management frameworks. The program culminates in a capstone case competition, allowing students to apply their skills in a real-world business scenario. All participants who complete the program will earn a Wharton Global Youth Certificate of Completion.

Title: Gilder Lehrman Institute Museum Internships
Summary: The Gilder Lehrman Institute's Summer Internship Program offers paid positions ($17 per hr) for high school, college, and graduate students. Participants gain experience in museum collection management, educational programming, development, marketing, and operations. Roles are available in remote, in-person, or hybrid formats.

Title: South Street Seaport Museum Internships
Summary: This 12-week summer program ($18 per hr) provides students with insight into museum operations and maritime history. Interns are typically placed in Collections, Archives, or Exhibitions, where they work on internal projects, visit other NYC institutions, and network with museum professionals.

Title: NY Historical Society Student Historian Internships
Summary: The New York Historical Society offers in-person internships where NYC high school students conduct in-depth research on American history. Interns create digital projects, meet with professional staff, and develop historical thinking and media skills centered on the theme, Our Composite Nation: Frederick Douglass' America. All interns will receive a stipend upon successful completion of the internship.

Title: Princeton Ten-Minute Play Contest
Summary: The Lewis Center for the Arts at Princeton University hosts an annual ten-minute playwriting contest for 11th-grade students. Each year, the competition is evaluated by a distinguished guest playwright, with past judges including acclaimed writers such as Anya Pearson, Jiehae Park, and Dipika Guha. This program provides high school juniors a unique opportunity to have their original dramatic work recognized by prominent professionals in the field of theater and playwriting.

Title: WashU Architecture Discovery Program
Summary: The Architecture Discovery Program (ADP) at Washington University in St. Louis is a rigorous 2-week introduction to architecture and design for high school students, featuring intensive individual instruction from Sam Fox School faculty. At the heart of the program is the Design Studio, which fosters creativity and discovery while exploring how sustainability and the built environment shape modern architectural practice. Through these explorations, participants develop high-quality material and technical skills to strengthen their professional design portfolios.

Title: John Locke Essay Competition
Summary: The John Locke Institute encourages young people to cultivate the characteristics that turn good students into great writers: independent thought, depth of knowledge, clear reasoning, critical analysis and persuasive style. The John Locke Institute Essay Competition invites students to submit original work across ten subject categories: Economics, History, International Relations, Law, Philosophy, Politics, Psychology, Public Policy, Science & Technology, and Theology. Evaluated by senior academics from institutions such as Oxford and Harvard, the contest emphasizes independent thought, critical analysis, and persuasive writing. Top winners in each category receive sizeable scholarships. Junior and senior entries are judged separately, totaling six awards per category. Winners will be recognized at an October 2026 ceremony in London.

Title: Walnut Hill Summer Theater Intensive
Summary: The Walnut Hill Summer Theater is a 3-week residential intensive where students develop theatrical skills through a balance of daily studio training and rehearsal. Participants take classes in acting, musical theater, and dance at the Delbridge Family Center for the Arts and are all cast in a single musical production performed over consecutive evenings. Located near Boston, the program includes dormitory living and staff-organized weekend excursions to iconic landmarks such as Faneuil Hall and the Museum of Fine Arts. Students conclude the program with strengthened performance abilities, increased confidence, and professional insight gained from immersive study and potential trips to professional theater productions.

Title: Girls Who Code Pathways Online Course
Summary: Pathways is a free online virtual learning program offering specialized curriculum tracks in game design, data science, AI, cybersecurity, and web development. Designed for girls and non-binary students in grades 9-12 (including rising 9th graders and graduating seniors), the program features a vibrant virtual community on Discord and access to advisor-led workshops, career panels, and corporate partner events. Over the course of 6-7 weeks, participants work at their own pace to complete technical projects aligned with emerging technologies.

Title: Ladder Internship Matching Program
Summary: Ladder Internships connects ambitious high school students with real startups for an 8-week summer internship. The program selects and trains interns before pairing them with host companies led by CEOs from institutions like Harvard Business School and Y-Combinator. This opportunity allows students to gain professional experience and mentorship from industry leaders who have held roles at top firms such as Google, Microsoft, and McKinsey.

Title: Writopia Advanced Writing Seminar at Pratt Institute
Summary: Writopia Lab offers a 2-week summer pre-college writing program at the Pratt Institute in Brooklyn, New York, open to rising high school juniors, seniors, and college freshmen. Students reside on campus and spend mornings in specialized tracks: Writing the City, Novel Writing, or Playwriting. In the afternoons, participants join multi-genre creative writing workshops led by professional writers, with an option for rising seniors to focus on college essays. Evenings and weekends feature literary activities, such as book clubs and film critiques, alongside optional excursions to various New York City landmarks.

Title: NYU Tandon Machine Learning Summer Program
Summary: This 2-week residential or commuter program introduces students to the computer science and mathematical techniques driving AI and machine learning. Lessons cover video and image recognition, autonomous vehicles, and medical diagnostics, providing fundamental knowledge of technologies that are integrated into daily life.

Title: NYU Coding for Game Design High School Summer Program
Summary: During this 2-week in-person course, students learn game design principles and C# scripting within the Unity engine. Participants work collaboratively and independently to create their own 2D games, following development techniques used by professional designers at NYU.

Title: Cornell Architecture & Design Summer Program
Summary: Cornell's College of Architecture, Art, and Planning (AAP) offers an intensive in-person summer program for high school students considering a bachelor's degree in architecture. This Introduction to Architecture and Design Precollege Program immerses participants in architectural ideas and methods through a studio-based environment. Working in small groups, students attend lectures and participate in specialized workshops focused on representational techniques and portfolio design. The program requires no prior specialized knowledge, only a serious interest in exploring architectural problems and design principles.

Title: Brown Pre-College Programs
Summary: Brown Pre-College offers 1- to 6-week residential programs designed to simulate the undergraduate experience without the pressure of formal grades. Students can choose from over 300 course offerings, ranging from medicine and law to visual arts and creative writing, while engaging in a community that values independent thinking and student voices.

Title: NYU Career Edge Summer Program
Summary: NYU Career Edge offers 1-week, non-credit intensives in professional fields like Criminal Justice, Entrepreneurship, and Finance. Designed for college and career readiness, the program allows students to explore career paths while experiencing life at a world-renowned university.

Title: NYU Precollege Courses
Summary: NYU Precollege allows rising juniors and seniors to take undergraduate courses taught by world-class faculty. Students immerse themselves in the dynamic NYU community, exploring potential majors and academic interests while interacting with classmates from around the world.

Title: Columbia Science Honors Program (SHP)
Summary: The Science Honors Program is a highly selective academic year program (September to May) for students with a strong interest in STEM. Classes are held at Columbia University on Saturdays from 10:00 AM to 12:30 PM. Courses are taught by active researchers and cover advanced topics in physical, chemical, biological, and computing sciences.

Title: Columbia Climate School in the Green Mountains
Summary: Based on a campus in the Green Mountains of Vermont, this 2-week program mobilizes high school students to address climate change. Participants engage with experts from the Columbia Climate School to learn about cutting-edge innovations, build partnerships with like-minded peers, and develop actionable strategies for driving environmental impact.

Title: Michigan Math & Science Scholars (MMSS) Summer Program
Summary: The Michigan Math and Science Scholars (MMSS) program is designed to offer a pre-college experience exposing students to a breadth of curricula offered at the University of Michigan while introducing high school students to current developments and research in the sciences. The program is open to rising high school sophomores, juniors, and seniors. Three 2-week sessions are offered; students are given the opportunity to attend one, two or all three sessions. MMSS features small ~15-student classes taught by University of Michigan faculty. Students take only one class per session and spend the majority of the day working with their class, spending time in research and computer laboratories, as well as doing field work with their professor. As a Residential Student, attendees will experience parts of the “college life” while living in an on-campus dorm room independently (with Counselor supervision), attending activities, pre-planned evening events and even optional weekend trips.

Title: Barnard NextGen Leadership Institute
Summary: The NextGen Leadership Institute at Barnard College offers a 3-week residential or commuter summer program in New York City for women. Participants select one of three academic tracks (STEMinist, Writing and Literature, or Global Humanities) and attend small classes led by Barnard faculty and expert instructors. The curriculum integrates traditional academic work, such as text analysis and experiments, with curated city-based learning experiences like museum visits and guest lectures. Additionally, the academic schedule is supplemented by a weekly Leadership in Action series focused on developing strategic thinking and collaborative skills.

Title: Barnard Athena Summer Innovation Institute
Summary: The Athena Summer Innovation Institute at Barnard College is a 3-week residential or commuter program for women focused on entrepreneurship and social impact. Operating as an intensive boot camp, the program places students in collaborative teams to develop new ventures, such as start-up businesses, non-profit organizations, or advocacy campaigns. Prior business ideas are not required, but participants must be motivated to create social good and learn about the startup process. Throughout the program, students receive coaching and mentorship from program leaders and participate in specialized workshops covering topics like financing, negotiation, and branding.

Title: Barnard Plate + Planet Lab
Summary: The Plate + Planet Lab at Barnard College is a 3-week residential or commuter program for women focused on the U.S. food system. Students examine food production, distribution, consumption, and waste management through the lenses of agriculture, health, policy and justice, climate change, and soil health. The curriculum includes hands-on learning via weekly visits to farms across New York City and New York State, guided by industry experts and professionals. The program aims to help students envision ecologically mindful food systems that support both communities and the environment.

Title: Wake Forest Sports Business Institute
Summary: The Sports Business Institute is a major highlight out of the 25 offerings at Wake Forest University's week-long Summer Immersion Program. Whether cold calling to bring together fans to support their favorite team, implementing promotions to enhance the game day experience, or negotiating sponsorship deals with Fortune 500 companies, students will learn about and get a behind-the-scenes look at the inner workings of this high-profile multi-billion dollar industry’s unique application to business principles. This institute explores career opportunities in both the collegiate and professional world, as guest speakers will further provide students with opportunities to walk away with an array of industry knowledge and a broad range of networking contacts.

Title: Cooper Union Introduction to Architecture Online Summer Course
Summary: The Cooper Union's Introduction to Architecture is an intensive, 5-week online program that introduces high school students to the discipline of architecture through an exploratory virtual environment. Rooted in the School of Architecture's unique studio ethic, the curriculum features rigorous foundation studies, history and practice lectures, and guided portfolio development to strengthen future applications to design schools. Students work closely with faculty and peers to develop technical skills and conceptual thinking. Admissions are conducted on a rolling basis, and early application is strongly encouraged.

Title: Interlochen Arts Camp
Summary: Join teens from around the world for an unforgettable summer at Interlochen Arts Camp, with a variety of programs ranging from 1-3 weeks in length. High school students in grades 9-12 dive into music, theatre, dance, visual arts, film, and creative writing. Learn from expert faculty, connect with new friends, and spend your summer fully immersed in an overnight arts camp experience that inspires creativity and prepares you for college and beyond.

Title: Fordham Summer Leaders Academy
Summary: The Fordham Summer Leaders Academy is a residential pre-college program in New York City lasting one to two weeks. It combines innovative academic courses with engaging co-curricular activities, offering both credit and non-credit opportunities in STEM, business, the humanities, and performing arts.

Title: Northwestern Debate Institute
Summary: The Northwestern Debate Institute offers a 4- to 6-week online program for high school policy debaters, designed to prepare participants for the upcoming season and beyond. Students learn the same fundamental principles and techniques that have led the Northwestern Debate Society to a record 15 National Debate Tournament championships. The program emphasizes personalized instruction through limited lab sizes and a low student-to-staff ratio, allowing debaters to engage with the nation's top competition. As the oldest and most successful debate society in NDT history, Northwestern offers an unparalleled opportunity for students to refine their skills under the guidance of elite coaches and scholars.

Title: Dialogues Virtual Clubs
Summary: The Dialogues program at Schoolhouse.world offers students a platform for 1-on-1 Zoom conversations designed to foster understanding rather than debate. Participants can engage in Dialogues Events for casual weekly chats on various topics or join Dialogues Clubs to build a consistent community with the same group of peers every other week. These sessions are free and come with discussion guides to help steer the conversation. A key benefit of the program is the Dialogues portfolio, which allows learners to demonstrate curiosity, empathy, and open-mindedness to partner colleges during the admissions process. Partner colleges include Columbia University, UChicago, and more.

Title: American Psychological Association (APA) Remote Internships
Summary: The APA Internal Internship Program is an online, year-round opportunity for U.S. high school students to explore the impact of psychology across fields such as research, policy, communications, and education. Participants apply psychological theory to practice in a professional setting, attending specialized workshops and connecting with industry experts. The program emphasizes the development of professional networks and the exploration of non-traditional psychology careers through discussions and group projects.

Title: EnergyMag Remote Internships
Summary: The EnergyMag Research Internship is a virtual program for high school students interested in exploring renewable energy companies, technologies, and markets. Open to sophomores, juniors, and seniors, the program helps students develop research, analytical, and professional writing skills. Under the guidance of mentors, participants produce publishable reports and gain experience in networking and communication. The program offers flexible scheduling to accommodate academic plans, including 2- to 8-week half-time summer internships and year-round quarter-time internships lasting 1 to 9 months. Successful participants receive a Letter of Accomplishment.

Title: Safe Haven Basketball Champions Special Needs Volunteers
Summary: The Safe Haven Basketball Champions Special Needs program is a coed initiative for children ages 4 to 16 with diverse developmental, social, and emotional abilities. The program meets on Sundays during the spring at PS 84 on West 92nd Street. Experienced basketball players are eligible to volunteer as Best Buddies, partnering with participants to help develop their athletic, social, and communication skills.

Title: West Side Soccer League EPIC Volunteers
Summary: The EPIC Division is an adaptive soccer program for children of all ages with physical and developmental challenges who require assistance to play. The league is coached by parents and volunteers, including teen buddies: experienced soccer players who serve as peer coaches and helpers. Those interested in volunteering as an EPIC Buddy can contact program coordinators Serhat Krause or Joshua Noble via the email addresses provided on the organization's website.

Title: Little League Challenger Division Volunteers
Summary: The Little League Challenger Division, established in 1989, is an adaptive baseball program for individuals with physical and intellectual challenges. The organization offers various community volunteer opportunities, such as serving as a player buddy, assisting with new player recruitment, and providing administrative or fundraising support. Those interested in volunteering can contact Director Sam Ranck using the email address provided on the organization's website.

Title: Friendship Circle NYC Teen Volunteers
Summary: Teen volunteers are paired with children and young adults with special needs to provide companionship and support. Opportunities include home visits and social outings throughout New York City, fostering inclusive communities through friendship.

Title: Justice Resource Center High School Programs
Summary: The Justice Resource Center offers a variety of civic and law-related programs to high school students. Whether students are building on their knowledge from elementary and middle school or are just discovering the world of law, JRC offers programs that help students become college and career ready. Students develop their potential by engaging in challenging law-related projects whereby they learn research, teamwork and critical thinking skills.

Title: NYU Stern EFL Young Ambassadors Entrepreneurship Program
Summary: This free program at the NYU Stern School of Business introduces NYC high schoolers to the world of startups and business. Selected students attend real-world startup conferences, shadow NYU MBA mentors, and learn directly from founders and investors. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis throughout the year.

Title: NYC Ranger Conservation Corps Internship
Summary: This 8-week environmental internship (offered in fall and spring) allows students to work with Urban Park Rangers on restoration projects in NYC’s flagship parks. Participants learn about urban ecology and may participate in field trips like canoeing and camping, earning community service hours for their college applications.

Title: NYC Health + Hospitals Volunteers
Summary: NYC Health + Hospitals offers ongoing volunteer opportunities for students at medical facilities across all five boroughs. Roles range from supporting pediatric patients to assisting the elderly, providing students with meaningful ways to contribute to community health and patient care.

Title: Sarah Lawrence Writers Week Summer Writing & Theatre
Summary: This week-long intensive program at Sarah Lawrence College focuses on creative writing and performance arts. Students collaborate with professional poets and prose writers to develop their craft, explore new genres, and share their work in a supportive, creative environment.

Title: Syracuse Summer College
Summary: For over 60 years, Syracuse University has offered high schoolers the chance to explore potential majors through 1- to 4-week courses. Students live in residence halls, dine on campus, and participate in social activities while taking college-level credit or non-credit courses. The Sports Management course is a major highlight, where students examine the managerial process, including the functions of management, and the roles, skills, and attributes required of sports managers.

Title: Transportation Alternatives Youth Activist Committee (TAYAC)
Summary: TAYAC is a community of teens advocating for car alternatives in NYC, focusing on public transit, biking, and walking. Open to all NYC youth, the committee holds monthly meetings and social events to help students lead local campaigns and improve the city’s transportation landscape.

Title: Manhattan School of Music Precollege Program
Summary: Manhattan School of Music’s Precollege program provides pre-conservatory training for talented musicians aged 8 to 18 through professional instruction and a supportive, collaborative environment. Held on Saturdays throughout the school year, the program offers two distinct tracks: the Classical Program and the Jazz Arts Program. Students engage in weekly private lessons and specialized coursework in theory, ear training, composition, orchestra, chorus, and conducting. In addition to rigorous academic and technical training, participants benefit from numerous performing opportunities in various recital halls and build lasting connections with a community of like-minded peers.

Title: Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) Discovery Guide Youth Volunteers
Summary: Young adults (ages 14-22) can volunteer as Discovery Guides at NYC’s five WCS zoos and aquarium. During spring or summer sessions, guides lead educational activities for visitors, support conservation campaigns, and assist with education programs while gaining experience in wildlife and environmental stewardship.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2026) will open in March

Title: Princeton Prize in Race Relations
Summary: The Princeton Prize in Race Relations recognizes high school students who have demonstrated exceptional leadership in advancing racial equity or promoting racial understanding within their schools and communities. Award recipients receive a $2,500 cash prize and an all-expenses-paid trip to Princeton University for a Symposium on Race, where they engage with fellow winners from across the country. Additionally, recipients are honored by Princeton alumni at recognition ceremonies held in their local regions.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for 2027) will open in October

Title: Studio Museum Expanding the Walls Photography Program
Summary: Teen Programs at the Studio Museum provide a supportive environment for students to express themselves creatively while developing essential communication and critical thinking skills. Participants have the opportunity to engage in tours, hands-on workshops, and discussions with prominent visual artists. The Expanding the Walls program is a free, 8-month, in-person initiative for high school students focused on photography, history, and community. The program culminates in a public celebration of student work. Participants receive a $1,000 stipend and a Canon EOS Rebel DSLR camera to support their creative development throughout the session.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for 2027) will open in September

Title: Brooklyn Museum Apprentice Program
Summary: In this paid internship, NYC high school students immerse themselves in art history and museum education at a world-class institution. Guided by curators and educators, apprentices create lesson plans and gain experience teaching audiences of all ages. Participants earn $16.50 per hour (rising to $17.50 for second-year leaders), work up to 180 hours annually, and receive MetroCards for travel.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Fall 2026) will open in July

Title: Stanford Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and Imaging (AIMI) Remote Internship
Summary: The Stanford Center for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and Imaging (AIMI) offers a 2-week online virtual summer internship for high school students interested in the intersection of AI and healthcare. Participants engage in specialized lectures, collaborate on research projects, and receive mentorship from Stanford researchers and students. The program features Virtual Career Lunch & Learns with guest speakers and offers an optional Student Lead role for those seeking additional leadership experience. Upon completion, students earn a certificate, with select participants becoming eligible for extended research opportunities.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open in December

Title: Mount Sinai Summer Junior Medical Program (JuMP)
Summary: The Junior Medical Program (JuMP) is a 6-week summer volunteering commitment (100 hours total) for students ages 15 to 17. Participants gain direct patient contact and observe the clinical and non-clinical daily operations of a hospital at Mount Sinai, learning from healthcare professionals to support patient satisfaction.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open in January

Title: Iowa Young Writers Studio Summer Residential Program
Summary: The 2-week Summer Residential Program at the University of Iowa in Iowa City offers an immersive creative writing experience for current 10th, 11th, and 12th-grade students. Participants select one core course (fiction, poetry, general creative writing, TV writing, or playwriting) taught by graduates of the Iowa Writers' Workshop and University of Iowa MFA programs. The curriculum emphasizes writing exercises, peer critique, and collaborative projects, and is supplemented by craft workshops, author readings, and social activities like open mics and talent shows.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open in January

Title: WCS Project TRUE (Teens Researching Urban Ecology) Internship
Summary: Project TRUE (Teens Researching Urban Ecology) is an urban ecology research and youth development program for high school sophomores and juniors living in the Bronx. Run by the Bronx Zoo Education team in partnership with Fordham University, the program provides hands-on field research experience.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open in January

Title: MIT MITES Summer
Summary: MITES Summer is a 6-week, on-campus program that immerses rising high school seniors from across the country in the MIT experience. Participants take five rigorous math, science, and humanities courses while developing the academic and personal skills necessary for success in STEM. In addition to coursework, the program features lab tours, social events, and dedicated college admissions counseling to provide firsthand insight into the rewards of pursuing STEM degrees and careers.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open in November

Title: BU Research in Science & Engineering (RISE)
Summary: The Research in Science & Engineering (RISE) program at Boston University is a 6-week residential program for rising seniors (currently enrolled in 11th grade). Students conduct university-level laboratory research and select either the Internship or Practicum track. The Internship track involves 40 hours per week of mentor-directed research focused on developing technical and analytical skills. Alternatively, the Practicum track consists of a daily two-hour morning lecture followed by four hours of collaborative group experiments designed to model standard university research procedures.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: Carnegie Hall Summer Youth Ensembles
Summary: Each summer, Carnegie Hall’s national youth ensembles bring together the brightest young American instrumentalists for intensive training and performances on some of the world’s greatest stages. All three programs are free and led by an all-star faculty of professional musicians, giving students the opportunity to hone their talents while working with the world’s finest artists. As national ensembles, these programs include a broad range of musicians from across the country that reflect the exceptional talent and diversity of the United States.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: Carnegie Mellon School of Drama Pre-College Program
Summary: The Carnegie Mellon University School of Drama Pre-College program is a 6-week residential program for high school juniors and seniors that offers training and preparation for college auditions and interviews within an acclaimed drama conservatory. Students choose from three specialized tracks: the Acting Option, which focuses on repertoire building and acting for the camera; the Design & Production Option, which concentrates on portfolio development and technical skills like stage management and fabrication; and the Music Theater Option, which prioritizes song coaching and tiered dance training in ballet and jazz. All students receive foundational instruction in dramaturgy, ensuring a comprehensive understanding of theatrical practice as they prepare for future applications to Bachelor of Fine Arts programs.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: Columbia Engineering the Next Generation (ENG)
Summary: This 6-week program at Columbia Engineering provides students with hands-on research experience and multi-level mentorship. Participants work alongside faculty and researchers to develop academic and professional skills in one of two tracks: the Foundations of Research (FoR) or the Center for Smart Streetscapes (CS3).
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: Columbia Summer High School Academic Program for Engineers (SHAPE)
Summary: SHAPE is a pre-college program for rising sophomores through recent graduates interested in STEM. Held at Columbia University, each 3-week session features college-level, project-based engineering courses taught by diverse faculty members.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: Kenyon Review Young Writers Workshops
Summary: The Kenyon Review Young Writers Summer Residential Workshops offer a dynamic 2-week residential program on the Kenyon College campus for talented high school students from around the world. Participants join a supportive literary community designed to stretch their creative talents and discover new strengths alongside peers who share a passion for the written word. These multi-genre workshops encourage students to challenge themselves through intensive writing exercises and collaborative sessions, all within the inspiring environment of a premier liberal arts institution.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: Manhattan District Attorney High School Internship Program (HSIP)
Summary: This rigorous 5-week internship offers students an insider’s perspective on the criminal justice system. Participants engage in workshops, professional development, and a mock trial program while working in an office setting. Interns are paid minimum wage and must demonstrate a strong interest in law and public service.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies (GISS) Internships
Summary: Students interested in climate science and data modeling can apply for a variety of research-based internships at the Goddard Institute for Space Studies. Interns work directly with NASA scientists on projects related to Earth science, gaining technical skills and exposure to professional research environments.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: NYU Applied Research in Science and Engineering (ARISE)
Summary: ARISE is a free 10-week summer program for students interested in STEM research. It consists of 4 weeks of foundational training in safety, writing, and research skills, followed by 6 weeks of hands-on research in over 80 NYU labs, where students assist faculty on real-world engineering and science projects.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: NYU Steinhardt Summer Art Intensive
Summary: In this 4-week summer program, high school artists develop their practice in digital art, painting, and sculpture. Students work closely with NYU faculty in a close-knit community to create ambitious works and gain insight into New York’s contemporary art world.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: NYU GSTEM Research Program
Summary: GSTEM is a 6-week summer research program for high school students interested in STEM careers. Participants are paired with researchers for individual projects in their chosen field, earn lab experience, and take weekly field trips to meet women leaders across various STEM disciplines.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program (SSRP)
Summary: SSRP is a competitive 7-week mentored research program for high school juniors and seniors. Scholars join research teams led by scientific trainees from Rockefeller University, MSK, and WCMC. The experience is supplemented by elective courses, guest lectures, and networking workshops.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: Telluride Association Summer Seminar
Summary: The Telluride Association Summer Seminar (TASS) is a free, 6-week educational program for high school sophomores and juniors focused on critical thinking and democratic community. The curriculum explores how power and privilege shape social structures through two distinct areas of study: TASS-CBS (Critical Black Studies), which examines history, politics, and art through the intellectual contributions of people of African descent, and TASS-AOS (Anti-Oppressive Studies), which investigates how diverse forms of power influence social organization. Held at Cornell University and the University of Maryland, the program covers all student costs, including tuition, books, room and board, and field trips. TASS is open to rising juniors and seniors who demonstrate a commitment to leadership and service, providing a transformative experience rooted in the humanities and social sciences.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: UChicago Summer Session Pre-College Program
Summary: The University of Chicago's Summer Session offers high school students the opportunity to join a global community of thinkers and engage with diverse subject areas in a rigorous academic environment. Situated on the university's Hyde Park campus, the program encourages students to take intellectual risks and explore topics beyond the high school curriculum. Residential programs range from one to four weeks in length. In the 3-Week Immersion, students enroll in an undergraduate-level course taught by UChicago faculty. These courses focus on in-depth exploration through seminar-style discussions, collaborative projects, and relevant field trips. The 4-Week Practicum involves intensive, hands-on courses are designed for students seeking deep research experience. Specialized tracks include Research in the Biological Sciences (RIBS), where participants learn advanced laboratory techniques, and Stones and Bones, a field-based program where students work alongside Field Museum paleontologists in Wyoming.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: Yale Young Global Scholars Summer Program
Summary: Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS) is an academic enrichment program designed for outstanding high school students from around the world. Each summer, participants from over 150 countries and all 50 U.S. states gather at Yale’s historic campus for a 2-week interdisciplinary residential session. The program provides an immersive global learning experience at Yale University, allowing students to engage with diverse perspectives and challenging academic content in a collaborative community. The curriculum is highly collaborative, exposing participants to innovative topics while facilitating student discussions shaped by international perspectives. Students have the opportunity to participate in a STEM, social sciences, humanities, or cross-disciplinary track.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: Urban Barcode DNA Research Program
Summary: The Urban Barcode Research Program (UBRP), supported by the Pinkerton Foundation, is a science education initiative that engages NYC high school students in biodiversity studies using DNA technology. Once accepted, students complete a training course in biodiversity, conservation biology, and research methodology, gaining hands-on experience with laboratory techniques. Under expert mentorship, participants then conduct student-driven research projects using DNA barcoding to explore the relationship between biodiversity and human activity. As members of the NYC Science Research Mentoring Consortium, students also gain access to collaborative events and programming at partnering scientific institutions.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for 26-27 Academic Year) will open in Spring 2026

Title: Whitney Museum Youth Insights Art Program
Summary: Youth Insights (YI) is an after-school and summer program that connects New York City high school students to art and artists. The Whitney also offers drop-in programs and events throughout the year.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for 2027) will open later this year

Title: Julliard Pre-College
Summary: Juilliard Pre-College provides high-quality preparatory instruction for students in orchestral instruments, piano, organ, classical guitar, classical voice, and composition. The curriculum includes private lessons, chamber music, music theory, ear training, and large ensembles, with electives available in conducting, music history, and other specialized topics. The Preparatory Education program runs on Saturdays from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM throughout the academic year, though students may occasionally be required to attend private lessons or chamber coachings during the week. Participants benefit from instruction by an outstanding faculty and receive numerous performance opportunities to refine their craft in a professional environment.
Deadline: Upcoming application cycle (for 2027) will open later this year

Title: Federal Reserve Bank High School Fed Challenge
Summary: The High School Fed Challenge is a research and writing competition designed to encourage students in grades 9-12 to explore economic themes and consider careers in the field. The program requires no previous study of economics, prioritizing intellectual curiosity and independent research. Participants gain a deeper understanding of economic principles and their real-world applications through the competition's annual theme, helping to foster critical thinking and analytical skills.
Deadline: Upcoming submission cycle (for 2027) will open in September

Title: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
Summary: The Scholastic Art & Writing Awards is the nation’s longest-running and most prestigious recognition program for creative teens in grades 7-12. This program provides an opportunity for students to submit original art and writing for the chance to earn local and national recognition, including scholarships and exhibition opportunities. In New York City, participants are eligible for Regional Awards, including Gold Key, Silver Key, and Honorable Mention distinctions, and are celebrated at a regional ceremony in March. Gold Key-winning works earn the additional honor of being showcased in the annual exhibition at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
Deadline: Upcoming submission cycle (for 2027) will open later this year

Title: C-SPAN StudentCam Documentary Competition
Summary: StudentCam is C-SPAN’s annual national video documentary competition that encourages students in grades 6-12 to think critically about issues affecting their communities and the nation. Participants must create a 5-6 minute documentary on a specified annual topic, incorporating C-SPAN video clips to support their research and analysis. The competition provides a platform for students to explore public policy and social issues while competing for various national prizes and recognition.
Deadline: Upcoming submission cycle (for 2027) will open later this year

Title: Bennington College Young Writers Awards
Summary: Bennington College in Vermont hosts the annual Young Writers Awards to recognize high school achievement in poetry, short stories, and essays. Open to students in grades 9-12 worldwide, the competition honors the college's literary legacy, which includes Pulitzer Prize winners and U.S. poet laureates. Submissions are due by November 1, with first, second, and third place winners selected alongside distinguished entries for each grade level. All recognized participants receive cash prizes and scholarships.
Deadline: Upcoming submission cycle will be due November 1, 2026

Title: NYC Parks Lifeguard Job
Summary: NYC Parks is seeking dedicated individuals (ages 16+) to serve as seasonal lifeguards at city pools and beaches in Summer 2026. This role offers a wage of $22.00 per hour and builds critical skills in safety and leadership. All applicants must pass a qualifying swim test and complete a training program.
Deadline: Upcoming qualifying swim tests (for Summer 2027) will begin in October

Title: NYC Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
Summary: As the nation’s largest youth employment program, SYEP connects NYC residents ages 14-24 with project-based learning opportunities or traditional 25-hour-per-week jobs. The program offers valuable work experience and financial compensation during the summer months.
Deadline: Upcoming submission cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: The Met Museum Internships
Summary: The Met offers paid summer internships for 10th and 11th grade students living in NYC. Interns explore museum careers in departments like curatorial, social media, design, and education. The program provides professional networking opportunities and hands-on work experience in a world-renowned art institution.
Deadline: Upcoming submission cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: Brooklyn District Attorney Summer Internship
Summary: The Brooklyn District Attorney’s 2026 Summer High School Internship offers an overview of one of the largest DA’s offices in the country. The program is only open to students who live in Brooklyn. Selected students will participate in workshops, tours, and presentations regarding law enforcement. An intern’s duties may include assisting in investigations, attending trials, preparing and compiling documents and financial data, conducting and analyzing legal research, and supporting community outreach programs. Students will receive a weekly stipend.
Deadline: Upcoming submission cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: Foreign Policy Research Institute (FPRI) Remote Internships
Summary: The FPRI Internship Program provides high school and college students with hands-on experience in the field of international relations. Interns support FPRI scholars by assisting with research or contributing to communications, events, and operations, with some roles requiring specialized skills in foreign languages or content creation. Participants receive mentorship from experienced professionals to develop critical thinking and collaboration skills, and they have the unique opportunity to publish original research on the program's Intern Corner. The experience is enriched by access to policy seminars and career-focused guest speaker sessions, including a weekly seminar series specifically for summer interns.
Deadline: Upcoming submission cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year

Title: Bank of America Student Leaders Program
Summary: Ladder Internships connects ambitious high school students with real startups for an 8-week summer internship. The program selects and trains interns before pairing them with host companies led by CEOs from institutions like Harvard Business School and Y-Combinator. This opportunity allows students to gain professional experience and mentorship from industry leaders who have held roles at top firms such as Google, Microsoft, and McKinsey.
Deadline: Upcoming submission cycle (for Summer 2027) will open later this year
